subject: MAP & Eval: Acceptance Anchors, Test Owners, and Close Plan (DataCrest)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amelia Chen <amelia@datacrest.ai>; Mark Torres <m.torres@datacrest.ai>
Date: 2026-11-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Draft MAP + initial acceptance anchors for review

Hi Amelia / Mark,

Thanks again for the time this morning — really excited about the pilot opportunity. Attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (DataCrest_MAP_v1.xlsx) that maps out a 6-week evaluation and close runway. I pulled together what I heard as your key success outcomes and added proposed owners and simple acceptance tests so we can avoid ambiguity during the pilot.

High-level anchors (please skim):
- Business outcome: 30% reduction in manual triage time on priority queues (sample of 5k cases)
- Latency target: p50 < 200ms, p95 < 800ms under a 1k RPS simulated load
- Accuracy/quality: precision on top-1 suggested action >= 88% on DataCrest validation set (n=1,200)
- Security/compliance: SOC2 evidence review + SSO provisioning (SAML) before production signoff

Requested from you: please add any missing acceptance tests (or reduce scope) and confirm who will be the internal SME(s) for data/IT/security. If these anchors look good I’ll turn this into the working MAP and propose milestone dates for the close timeline.

Attachments: DataCrest_MAP_v1.xlsx, MAP-test-cases.csv

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Mark Torres <m.torres@datacrest.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Amelia Chen <amelia@datacrest.ai>
Date: 2026-11-06T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP + initial acceptance anchors for review

Ben — thanks for this. Good start. A few quick notes from our side: 

1) Timeline: 6 weeks sounds reasonable but can we compress the integration window to 3 weeks if we run the data export in parallel? We can commit engineering time for that.
2) Quality anchor: 88% precision is fine, but we also need a recall floor (>= 75%) — we care about not missing high-severity items.
3) Security: we’ll need a short evidence packet for vendor risk (our InfoSec team uses a standard template). I attached the SOC2-itemized-request.pdf with specific items we need.

We’ll add our SME names once I sync with IT tomorrow. Also — please add a simple rollback/stop condition in the MAP (e.g., precision drops >6% between demo and final run).

Best,
Mark
Director, Automation & Platform | DataCrest
m.torres@datacrest.ai

Mark — perfect, appreciate the specificity. I updated the MAP and slid in the rollback/stop condition you suggested. Key edits (see DataCrest_MAP_v1.xlsx v1.1 on Drive):

- Timeline: added an accelerated lane if DataCrest can provide bulk export + test tokens within 72 hours of SOW signature (new milestone A1).
- Quality: added recall >= 75% as a second acceptance metric; consolidated pass/fail for final acceptance (both precision >= 88% AND recall >= 75%).
- Performance: added a smoke-test plan (MAP-test-cases.csv) — owners and run-book steps included.
- Security: noted the SOC2 items you flagged and assigned our security liaison (priyom_das) to coordinate evidence transfer.
- Exit gates (proposed):
   1) Integration sanity: sample ingest + model inference validated on 200 records (owner: DataCrest Eng)
   2) Security signoff: InfoSec items validated or scheduled with KRs (owner: priyom_das)
   3) Demo acceptance: pilot demo where DataCrest product leads validate suggested-action precision/recall against the validation set (owner: lauren_bishop)
   4) SLA and cutover checklist agreed + DocuSign of SOW amendments (owner: ben_carter)

Action items for this week (proposed):
- Data export + tokenized sample (DataCrest) — target: 2026-11-09
- Security evidence pickup (Redwood/Prioyam) — target: 2026-11-10
- Smoke test run (Redwood) — target: 2026-11-11

I’ve also added a simple pass/fail rubric to the sheet that maps each acceptance test to an owner, test data, and success threshold. If you confirm owners by end of tomorrow I’ll convert the MAP into the shared working spreadsheet and open an owners-only tab for test artifacts.

Thanks — I’ll book a 30-min sync for Thursday morning to align on owners and the accelerated lane.

Ben
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Internal: Quick runbook review before DataCrest sync (Thursday)

Folks —

Short internal note before I present the MAP to DataCrest on Thursday: please review the smoke-test steps in MAP-test-cases.csv and confirm you own the following items by Wednesday EOD: 

1) lauren_bishop: lead the demo script and define the acceptance checklist for the demo (what 'validated' looks like).
2) jordan_blake: be ready to run the accelerated integration lane and coordinate with DataCrest Eng for the bulk export; I’ll send the sample ingestion steps.
3) priyom_das: confirm we can deliver the SOC2 items they requested and outline any gaps (call out anything that requires >1 week).

Stop/rollback triggers to flag during the run (for the audience):
- Regression: final precision drop >6% vs demo run OR recall < 72% at final run -> pause rollout and schedule immediate root-cause sync.
- Latency: p95 > 1.2s on a 1k-RPS sim -> pause acceptance and enable fallback routing to smaller batch model.

I’ll incorporate any edits and post a final MAP doc to the Drive. If we hit the accelerated lane we could potentially close in 4 weeks instead of 6 — but we need irons in the fire (owners + sample data).

Thanks — short call Thursday 10am PT.

Ben
